Good question.

On the 5-minute window they get a hard error from the OAuth callback: `Snowflake OAuth callback timeout - authorization took too long`. The local callback server is closed via the authorize-scope finalizer, so the port is released.

There is no mid-flow resume after that timeout: the failed attempt is discarded. Starting Login with Snowflake again runs a fresh `authorize` (new PKCE, state, and `127.0.0.1` listener), so the flow restarts cleanly without leftover callback state from the timed-out attempt.

This may have been fixed in 1.18.15 actually

This was addressed in the latest release by changing compaction requests so the conversation history is serialized into a single user message. This prevents preserved assistant `thinking` / `redacted_thinking` blocks from being modified or replayed as part of the compaction request.

We also verified the post-compaction path with Amazon Bedrock Claude Opus 4.6 and thinking enabled, including retained recent turns, a tail beginning at an assistant-message boundary, and multiple messages sent after compaction. We could not reproduce the failure on the latest release.

Closing as resolved. If you continue to hit this on the latest version, please let us know with updated reproduction details and we can reopen the issue.

I ran into this issue while building an orchestration framework on top of OpenCode and wanted to share what I found after tracing the implementation.

Initially I assumed this was a bug because I was requesting a Medium model for a delegated Worker task, but the Worker was executing with MiMo.

After inspecting the framework, I realized the behavior was actually expected:

* Agent-configured models are propagated correctly.
* `SubtaskPart.model` is supported.
* The HTTP Prompt API supports explicit model selection.
* The Task tool itself does **not** expose a runtime `model` parameter, so there is no supported per-invocation override.

The real problem in my framework turned out to be that the Director was still delegating to the generic `worker` alias instead of `worker-medium`. Since `worker` was configured with MiMo, the runtime was behaving correctly.

Changing the delegation to explicit capability-based agents (`worker-small`, `worker-medium`, `worker-large`) solved the problem without any changes to OpenCode.

So I can confirm that this is not a runtime bug—the current implementation is internally consistent.

Although I still think a runtime model override could simplify orchestration frameworks by reducing duplicated agent definitions, the current capability-based approach works well once the routing is configured correctly.

Hopefully this investigation helps anyone who arrives here after assuming the model selection is being ignored, as I initially did.

Same issue here — paying **OpenCode Go** subscriber, all Go-tier models blocked since 2026-07-22 while free models work.

**Verified reproduction (own account):**

- `GET /zen/go/v1/models` → `200 OK` (key valid, full model list)
- `POST /zen/go/v1/chat/completions` (model `deepseek-v4-flash`) → `401` `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"AuthError","message":"Request blocked by upstream provider."}}`

**Account state:** Go subscription active, all usage limits (hourly/weekly/monthly) sufficient, API key valid — also tried a freshly generated key, same result. `/v1/models` works while `chat/completions` is blocked, so the key itself is fine; the block happens server-side on the upstream provider call.

Affected models (all same error): `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash`, `kimi-k2.6`, `glm-5.2`, `minimax-m3`, etc.

Paying users are currently unable to use the service they subscribe to. Any update / ETA on a fix, and will there be compensation (prorated refund) for the downtime?

After two separate days of investigating this issue, I accidentally discovered that the Web UI is actually working as intended.

I'm closing the issue, but I want to document what happened because other users have reported similar behavior, and I think there are some UI/UX improvements that could prevent this confusion.

## What initially looked broken

When opening the Web UI without any project added, the initial screen instructs the user to **open a session to get started**.

However, clicking the **+ / New Session** button appears to do absolutely nothing: no navigation, no error, no toast, and no other feedback.

At the same time, opening **Add project** shows **"No folders found"**. There is no clear indication that the user is expected to start typing a filesystem path in order to search for a project.

This combination made it look like the Web UI was unable to communicate correctly with the server or access its filesystem.

## What I discovered

The missing step was simply that a project must be **explicitly added/selected before a session can be created**.

In the **Add project** dialog, typing a path such as `/my-folder/` causes matching directories to appear. After selecting one:

- the project appears on the Home screen;
- the **New Session** action becomes available;
- the **+ / New Session** button works;
- sessions are created and the agent responds normally.

I discovered this accidentally after two days of debugging.

While testing a code change that automatically added a project, I noticed that New Session suddenly worked. When I removed that automatically added project, it stopped working again.

That led me to manually add a project in my original, completely unmodified self-hosted instance and everything worked.

So I confirmed that **no code change was actually necessary**.

## About `/new`

In my original report I also mentioned that manually opening:

`https://<server>/new`

created a session, but messages sent from that session never started the agent. The user message was stored, but no assistant response was generated.

We now understand why.

By manually navigating to `/new`, I was effectively **forcing the application into the new-session flow without having a valid project selected**. This bypassed the normal UI flow that prevents creating a session when there is no project context.

In my case, this resulted in a session associated with an invalid/nonexistent directory (we observed a corrupted directory value such as `/��`). The session existed, but it had no valid project/workspace context for the agent to operate in.

So this behavior was another consequence of entering the new-session route without a project, rather than evidence that session execution itself was broken.

I do think this route could use some defensive handling. If `/new` is opened without a valid project, the UI could:

- redirect to Home;
- disable the prompt;
- show a toast/message asking the user to select a project;
- or otherwise prevent an invalid session from being created.

## UI/UX feedback

Although this turned out not to be a functional bug, I think the current UX makes it **very easy to interpret the expected behavior as a broken Web UI**, especially for a first-time user.

I believe this was the main reason I initially concluded there was a bug, and it may explain why other users are reporting similar symptoms.

A few small changes could make the flow much clearer:

- **Initial empty state:** instead of telling the user to "open a session to get started" when no project exists, instruct them to **add/select a project first**. Currently the UI asks the user to perform an action that cannot succeed yet.

- **Add project dialog:** instead of only displaying **"No folders found"**, show something like **"Start typing a path to search for a project"**.
